note: Reported defects from the engagement brief are tracked as hypotheses. Status reflects what has been reproduced/fixed against the current working tree, not the audited baseline. Live gates are BLOCKED, never PASSED, without an authorized workspace.

findings.title: Malformed name/schedule YAML breaks the whole bundle
findings.evidence: Line 187 collapsed `schedule:` onto the `name:` value line for the formula_prioritization job. `yaml.safe_load_all` fails at line 187: 'expected <block end>, but found <scalar>'. A single unparseable resource file means `databricks bundle validate/deploy` cannot load any job.
findings.fix: Split the `name` and `schedule` keys onto separate lines with correct indentation.

findings.title: Duplicate YAML keys silently override jobs/pipelines
findings.evidence: A duplicate mapping key is silently accepted by a plain safe_load, so a second job under an existing key would erase the first. Checked with a duplicate-rejecting loader across all bundle files.
findings.fix: No duplicate keys present in current tree; guard added to prevent regression.

findings.title: Referenced notebook paths must all resolve
findings.evidence: 133 notebook_path references checked against the filesystem; 0 missing.

findings.title: Setup notebooks must be re-runnable as idempotent upgrades without data loss
findings.evidence: The platform has no separate migration tool; the setup notebooks are both the clean install and the upgrade path. Audited their DDL: all CREATE TABLE use IF NOT EXISTS (175 idempotent statements), existing-deployment column upgrades use ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS IF NOT EXISTS (e.g. response_actions finding_id/approved_finding_revision), and there is no CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE or DROP TABLE. The idempotent-upgrade property already holds; no new parallel migration hierarchy was added (would duplicate the existing pattern). A guard now locks the property.

findings.title: Deployed serverless notebooks use serverless-incompatible Spark APIs
findings.evidence: Deployment-aware audit mapped jobs whose environment spec sets environment_version (serverless) to the notebooks they deploy, then scanned those files. Four deployed serverless notebooks used APIs serverless does not expose (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/limitations): streaming_correlation, temporal_window_correlator and graph_neighborhood used spark.sparkContext.broadcast; trend_engine_cet used spark.sparkContext.setCheckpointDir and imports GraphFrames (a JVM library, absent from its serverless dependency list).
findings.fix: Replaced the three broadcast lookups with plain closure capture (Spark serializes captured Python objects to executors), which is semantically identical for the small baseline/projection maps and offline-verified clean. trend_engine_cet cannot be fixed by a Python edit: GraphFrames + RDD checkpointing require classic compute, so its serverless-to-classic migration is tracked as BLOCKED pending staging validation and allowlisted in the regression.

findings.evidence: Prior session unified deterministic content-addressed IDs over Kafka coordinates across the streaming and durable paths.

findings.title: Threat-intel match persisted before nonrecoverable alert emission
findings.evidence: Reported match-written/alert-missing recovery gap. The offline fault-injection regression cannot import the real logic: notebooks/detection/02_threat_intel_matching.py runs dbutils.widgets and spark.sql at module top level, so it is not importable without a live runtime. Reproducing this offline needs the match-persist/alert-emit step extracted into an importable _shared helper (a streaming-detector refactor) or a Databricks workspace; not attempted blind to preserve detector semantics.

findings.title: UEO revisions not bound through FUSE/Confluence/findings/approvals
findings.evidence: Prior session switched UEO writes to a revision-bumping MERGE upsert and added invalidate_revision + _invalidate_findings to WITHDRAW the bound finding when evidence changes. Full FUSE->verdict->approval fencing chain still to be proven end to end.

findings.title: Health could report healthy over a degraded/empty run; _config vs _cfg
findings.evidence: Confirmed a live defect: Monitor.report_health referenced self._cfg while __init__ stored self._config, so every call raised AttributeError, which a bare `except: pass` swallowed -- pipeline_health was never written yet log_complete believed it reported 'healthy'. Fixed self._cfg -> self._config and replaced the silent swallow with logger.exception so a health-write failure is visible. Regression imports the real monitoring module (via an import-boundary pyspark shim) and asserts (1) report_health issues exactly one MERGE into pipeline_health, (2) a failing write is logged at ERROR not swallowed, (3) log_complete drives a health write. This complements the prior-session UEO harvest health work (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE).

findings.title: Tool args ordered by dict insertion; no schema validation before SQL
findings.evidence: Prior session added _validate_and_order_args: orders by parameters.properties and rejects unknown/missing-required/type/enum before spark.sql.
findings.regression: tests/security/test_tool_arg_validation.py (imports the real BaseAgent validators; pins schema-order emission, unknown/missing/type/enum rejection, NULL padding for omitted optionals, and SQL-literal escaping of crafted strings)

findings.evidence: Prior session built an entry-only suite: writes only to Kafka/landing, asserts only on published outputs, 10 required scenarios, per-scenario probe isolation. Offline contract passes; live run BLOCKED pending workspace.
